title: Tool routing evaluator and argument sanity suite
creator: Marco Li
description: Build an automated evaluation harness that measures tool/function-selection accuracy and argument validation quality across config and model changes. This ticket focuses on a testable pipeline that ties model/config diffs to measurable regressions, produces per-commit alerts, and surfaces concrete rollback or mitigation suggestions.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic harness runs on CI for every model/config change and emits a pass/fail + metrics for tool selection accuracy (top-1/top-3) and argument field validation coverage.
Per-commit regression alerts are created when selection accuracy drops >3% absolute or when required argument validation failures increase by >5% compared to the baseline.
Dashboard visualizes per-model, per-config delta and highlights offending prompts and example traces for debugging.
Runbook with rollback/mitigation suggestions is generated automatically for any alert (e.g., pin model to previous version, fallback routing rule, or disable specific tool flag).
End-to-end tests included that simulate common failure modes: ambiguous tool names, partial argument omission, and malicious/incorrect arg types.
implementation_notes: Leverage existing eval harness infra used by evals-team but extend with a tool-routing comparator module that computes top-k correctness and argument validation pass rates.
Store ground-truth tool labels and canonical argument schemas in the eval dataset metadata; allow sample-level 'expected_args' overrides for edge cases.
Run lightweight execution of validated arguments in sandboxed function stubs to confirm runtime compatibility (no external side-effects).
Add a config diff hook in deploy pipeline that triggers the harness when model, quantization profile, or routing policy changes.
test_plan: Unit tests for comparator logic (deterministic top-k scoring).
Integration test that runs the harness on a seeded set of 10k prompts and verifies metric stability vs baseline.
Canary job in staging that runs on nightly model upgrades and asserts no regressions before promoting to production.
Simulated failure injection tests: rename tool labels, strip args, and feed malformed JSON to ensure alerting fires.
monitoring: Create Grafana panel: 'tool_selection_accuracy_by_model' with top-1/top-3 lines and delta band against baseline.
Alert rule in PagerDuty when accuracy delta <= -3% or argument-validation-fail-rate increases by >5% over 24h.
SLO: 99.5% of deployments must pass the harness in staging before promotion.
Log retention: store failing examples with full trace for 90 days for postmortems.
progress_updates: 2025-02-15: Kickoff meeting with Evals, Runtime, and Console. Agreed scope and baseline metrics.
2025-02-17: Initial comparator prototype implemented; local run shows selection top-1 scoring working on a 2k-sample set.
2025-02-19: Hooked pipeline trigger into model-change webhook; first CI job runs but false positives observed for tools with overlapping names.
2025-02-20: Implemented name-disambiguation heuristics and argument schema strictness toggle; reduced false positives by 40%.
decisions: Choose a conservative default: wallet a 3% absolute drop threshold for alerts to balance noise vs sensitivity.
Sandboxed argument execution will use no-network micro-stubs to avoid side-effects; full execution reserved for on-call manual repro.
Store baselines per-customer segment for Dedicated/Private customers to avoid cross-customer noise.
risks: False positives on selection accuracy due to ambiguous prompt phrasing; mitigated by expanding evaluation prompt templates.
Running stubs at scale adds compute costs; we will sample at 10% by default and prioritize failing prompts.
Tightly-coupled to model metadata cleanliness — will add a validation step in model onboarding to reduce bad labels.
notes: Follow-up: schedule a cross-team review with Solutions Engineering to validate customer-facing runbook recommendations.
Potential follow-on: integrate with Optimize to suggest quantization/config pairs that avoid routing regressions.
